notes: University layer: the Syllabus Minimum Requirements Policy now requires an AI usage policy in every syllabus (instructor discretion); the May 2026 Faculty Senate draft of this requirement (https://senate.oregonstate.edu/sites/senate.oregonstate.edu/files/2026-05/26%2005%20Faculty%20Senate%20-%20Draft%20AI%20Syllabus%20Statement%20Policy.pdf) was fetched but excluded as superseded by the adopted policy. The CTL syllabus-statement page is a public Canvas page fetched via the Canvas pages API route (canonical page URL https://canvas.oregonstate.edu/courses/1965953/pages/ctl-guidance-for-syllabus-statements-about-ai-use). Ecampus guidelines are a PDF; pypdf extracts it one word per line, so coders should match anchors across line breaks. The EECS graduate handbook is mostly program requirements; only Section 2.21 is AI policy. Excluded: ai.oregonstate.edu/guidelines (hub of links plus tool/data-classification list, no teaching policy text of its own); CTL Canvas page of faculty-submitted sample statements (collection of other instructors' examples). No separate AI or data-science computing unit found: AI and CS degrees sit inside EECS. Course layer: the EECS Fall 2026 class list (classes.engr.oregonstate.edu/eecs/) links no public course sites, Ecampus syllabi are 'available in Canvas to students enrolled', and searches for CS 161/162/261/290 syllabi found none public, so course policies are behind Canvas login (inaccessible).
